newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

CANADA, March 17 - Vancouver, B.C. - GRAIN - 4 Vessels loading, 18 waiting. Delays depending on grade to be loaded and up to 3 weeks. Some vessels now being nominated for April, mostly for PRC. Eight vessels still due before end of March. Roberts Bank - COAL - 2 Vessels loading today, 7 waiting, 11 due before the end of March. 23 Positions already nominated for April. Prince Rupert - GRAIN - 1 Vessel loading today, 10 waiting. Railcars now arriving regularly. Intention is to load one wheat vessel every 4 days up to the end of March, as well as barley vessels in between. Halifax, N.S. - No congestion or delays. Port is ice free. Halifax and Dartmouth ship yards available for ship repairs. New breakbulk facility, pier A, plans to open in spring 1997.

EL SALVADOR, March 14 - Acajutla - 2 Vessels loading bagged sugar at berth, 3 discharging at berth (1 corn,soya, 1 bagged fertiliser, 1 petroleum products). 1 Vessel waiting at anchorage to discharge fuel oil. 18 Vessels due by 3/4 of which 14 to discharge (1 palm oil, 1 corn/soya, 1 petroleum, 1 butane gas, 1 tallow/soya oil, 1 corn, 1 bulk sulphate, 2 bulk fertiliser, 2 full containers, 1 corn/wheat/rice, 1 bagged ammonium sulphate, 1 general cargo). 1 To discharge/load containers, 2 to load (1 coffee, 1 bulk sugar), 1 general cargo/containers. Delays dependent on weather.

MEXICO, March 18 - All ports working normally. Tampico - Eight vessels in port of which 1 cement, 2 minerals, 1 scrap, 2 general cargo, 1 sugar, 1 asphalt, 1 anchored awaiting instructions. Altamira - Six vessels in port of which 2 containers, 3 chemicals, 1 under repair, 2 anchored discharging vcm. Veracruz - 10 Vessels in port of which 3 sugar, 3 grain, 2 chemicals, 1 pipes, 1 general cargo. Manzanillo - Seven vessels in port of which 2 containers, 1 steel coils, 3 grain, 1 general cargo. Coatzacoalcos - 17 Vessels in port of which 7 chemicals, 9 oil tankers, 1 under repair.

UNITED STATES, March 18 - Jersey City, NJ, Cartaret, NJ, Perth Amboy, NJ - No vessels. Port Newark, NJ - One vessel in port. Port Elizabeth, NJ - Four vessels in port. Bayway, NJ - One vessel in port. Northern ports - New Jersey - Working normally, no congestion/delays. Baltimore - Port normal. Eight bulkers, 3 container, 2 ro-ros, 2 auto, 2 tankers, 4 general cargo, 1 cable vessel on stand-by, 2 vessels in repair yard, 3 bulkers awaiting berths of which 2 to discharge sugar, 1 under arrest.

Hampton Roads, VA - Four general cargo/container vessels berthed and operating, 3 bulkers loading coal, 1 waiting to load, 1 tanker lightering crude into barges, 1 bulker loading woodpulp. 3 vessels berthed under repair, 1 anchored under repair, 1 on layberth. Honolulu, HI - Honolulu harbour 2 container vessels, 4 tugs and barges berthed, no vessels at anchorage, Barber's Point -2 barges berthed. Off port moorings 2 tankers.

EAST COAST - Baltimore, MD - No congestion at Dundalk terminal. Clear at C and D canal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling. No delays at elevators and coal operations. Consol coal - Average waiting time 4 days. Liquid bulk facilities - Normal. No congestion. Anchorage available at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC - No vessels due at shipyard coal terminal or grain elevator. No delays expected at tanker terminals, light at Columbus street, north Charleston and Wando terminals. Dredging continues in main channel,no navigation problems.

Jacksonville, FL - No heavy berth congestion or delays at the port or Fernandina Beach. St. John's bar pilots determined new controlling draft in the St. John's river from 600 ft. south of buoy 75a to the end of the terminal channel to 30 ft. 06 in. Fw. This refers to operation of vessels in channel only. Vessels may also be limited by depth of water at their berth. Miami, FL - No congestion at container berths, gantry and ro-ro berths are available all week. Passenger terminals in full operation. Dates and times for dredging operations by army corps of engineers unchanged. New York, NY - No congestion at anchorages, container, tanker terminals. sugar terminals congestion.

Norfolk, VA - 21 Vessels due during week. 2 Vessels anchored waiting to load, 99 due at Dominion terminal, 2 anchored waiting to load. 5 Due at pier IX coal terminal. Norfolk southern coal pier - Will undertake scheduled maintenance to the no. 1 ship loading system from 8/4 to 29/4. No vessels due at Cargill. On 13/3, vessel made contact with the container berth at the international terminal. Portion of the berth will be out of service until damages are determined and repaired. Last week 2 other vessels had a minor collision at the mouth of Chesapeake bay. Otherwise container and general cargo terminals working normally, no other delays. Oil and other bulk terminals operating with channel open and prevailing depths available. Crane no. 7 is out of service until 18-19/3. Upgrades to the lifting and trollying abilities at crane nos. 6 and 7 will take place and will be completed by 30/6.

Philadelphia, PA - No congestion in port or at Camden, Wilmington. Savannah, GA - Heavy congestion expected in the latter part of week at Garden City terminals, heavy congestion mid week at Ocean terminals, no delays at east coast terminal. Sugar refinery busy, 2 vessels and a barge due, all liquid bulk facilities operating normally, no congestion expected. Navigation normal, vessels may expect delays due to fog.

GULF COAST - Houston, TX - No congestion at city docks, Cargill, Houston public grain elevator and Farmland grain elevator. Galveston - Congestion in some oil/chemical terminals. Fog every morning. Mobile, AL - No congestion in port. New Orleans, LA - Rain delayed grain loading. River stage at 15.5 ft, expect to be 17 ft. by 23/3. Normal transit times expected. Mississippi river drafts unchanged.

WEST COAST - Columbia River - 14 Grain vessels in port of which 7 loading, 7 waiting, waiting time 3-5 days. Coos bay, OR - Vessel traffic slow in past week, woodchip carriers loading, 1 lumber vessel due to load forest products for Australia. Log vessels expected to increase in coming weeks. No delays due to weather. Honolulu, HI - Light traffic expected at Barbers Point harbour and Honolulu harbour. Pier 40 demolition and construction project has begun, during demolition vessels should stay clear of area.

Long Beach, CA - Metropolitan delays 1-2 days expected at anchor awaiting berth. Koch Carbon - 3 Vessels due in March, no delays expected. Kaiser - Moderate for March, 1-2 days delay expected awaiting berth. March looks moderate in Los Angeles, Long Beach harbour for bulk cargoes. San Francisco, CA - Stockton still operating under reduced transit draft restrictions. For pilots, maximum transit draft for vessels to and from Stockton is 30 ft. 6 in. Controlling depth for Sacramento deep water ship channel changed to 24 ft at zero tide, with max freshwater draft of 27 ft. Meeting 16/3 to discuss shoaling that has taken place in the river ports and how best to work towards solution. Dredging continues, more soundings to be taken. Anchorages clear, little fog. Delays expected at Stockkton and Sacramento due to shoaling and dredging.
